question: Can Parpola 2019 text no. 7 bridge the H-940/H-2147/H-2148 obverse recurrence and M-77, or does it expose a sign-list/scope problem?
result: It exposes a sign-list and scope problem. Parpola text no. 7 is source-located as M-2109/M-2111 in Figure 1 and is explicitly standardized rather than raw rod imagery. Parpola says sign no. 107 ends text no. 7, later says text no. 7 is not as such attested in seals and that M-35 is the seal form without final 107, while the earlier recurrence paragraph also names M-77. The local Lipi and Mayig layers do not line these claims up as exact strings: M-2109/M-2111 are +400-000-220-415+, H companions are +520-220-415+ or stress variants, M-35 is seven signs, and M-77 is five signs.

parpola_constraints.figure_policy: Figure 1 uses standardized signs and not actual rod shapes; actual shapes require CISI photos.
parpola_constraints.text_no_7_sequence_status: Figure 1 row 7 gives visual standardized signs, but the prose does not provide a full explicit numeric sequence for text no. 7.
parpola_constraints.text_no_7_final: Parpola sign no. 107 uniquely ends text no. 7.
parpola_constraints.h_controls: Without sign no. 107, the remaining part occurs on H-938/H-939/H-1284/H-2145; H-940/H-2147/H-2148 have sign no. 41 on reverse and related obverse text.
parpola_constraints.seal_scope: Conclusion says text no. 7 is not as such attested in seals; without the last sign it forms M-35. Earlier recurrence paragraph names M-77 in the H-obverse context.

next_gate: Acquire or locate a sign-number transcription bridge for Parpola text no. 7, M-35, M-77, and the H obverse controls. Keep H-2148 reverse sign-no.-41 same-side identity separate from this obverse recurrence scope problem.
